learning_outcomes.text: To gain basic knowledge related with the fluids and their behavior patterns
Learning how to make material, momentum and energy balances in flow systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Unit systems and dimensional analysis. Basic concepts related with fluids. Fluid mechanics, state functions for gases, objectives of fluid mechanics.
Fluid statics. Pressure, force balance, hydrostatic equilibrium. Decanters, centrifuges, manometers. Buoyancy force applications.
Fluid statics. Pressure, force balance, hydrostatic equilibrium. Decanters, centrifuges, manometers. Buoyancy force applications.
Fluid flow. Transfer in molecular level. Velocity gradient, viscosity, types of fluids. Boundary layer, boundary layer separation, Equivalent diameter.
Fluid flow. Transfer in molecular level. Velocity gradient, viscosity, types of fluids. Boundary layer, boundary layer separation, Equivalent diameter.
Laminar flow, shell-momentum balance in rectangular, cylindrical and spherical coordinates. Total mass, momentum and energy balances.
Laminar flow, shell-momentum balance in rectangular, cylindrical and spherical coordinates. Total mass, momentum and energy balances.
Incompressible fluids. Mechanical energy balance, pressure drop, Bernoulli equation, friction losses, shaft work. Laminar and turbulent flow and design equations of pipelines.
Incompressible fluids. Mechanical energy balance, pressure drop, Bernoulli equation, friction losses, shaft work. Laminar and turbulent flow and design equations of pipelines.
Flow of compressible fluids. Isothermal flow, adiabatic flow and Mach number.
Fluid flow measurement, venture meters, orifice, rotameters, weirs.
Pumps and gas driving equipment. Pumps and NPSH, compressors (adiabatic, isothermal), fans and blowers.
Fluid flow around immersed bodies. Drag coefficient and drag force. Flow over sphere, long cylinder and disc. Behaviors of bodies in fluids. Flow in packed beds and fluidized beds.
Agitators, types of agitators, geometric factors. Vortex formation. Calculation of power requirement of an agitator.
